title: Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

items.topic: CMS integration blocked on open questions
items.statement: Kobi stated that the CMS integration open questions, the deal unique-makeup questions and CMS sandbox access must be sorted out before Jumpr is unblocked to build the integration.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … I think the the main thing I want to go through today was like figuring out the the CMS integration pieces and the open questions and uh and like the questions that have uh or the kind of worms that have opened up with the deals and their unique makeup as a result. I think if we can sort through that then um and sandbox access for CMS we will be unblocked

items.topic: Player auto-activates on signup completion
items.statement: Kobi reported that the player lifecycle is in place: when a signup is completed, the player is automatically activated from Pending status.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … the player life cycle should be good now. So when a signup is completed, it'll activate the player automatically from pending status.

items.topic: Inactive automation after 90 days
items.statement: Kobi reported an automation that moves a player to Inactive when there has been no signup for 90 days; he believed it may still be set to two days for testing.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … we also added the automation to move them to inactive if it's been if there's been no sign up for the last 90 days. Um, I believe right now it might still be set to like two days just for testing purposes.

items.topic: Ban automation keeps players banned
items.statement: Kobi reported that when a player is banned, signups still flow through but the player is not moved to Active and stays banned until manually unbanned.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … and then the ban automation, like if you ban somebody, uh, the signups will still flow through. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, it none of that is going to get blocked, but it won't it won't necessarily move the player to an active status. So they'll still remain banned until they're manually unbanned.

items.topic: Ban/pause reactivation logic for referrers
items.statement: Kobi reported that ban/pause reactivation logic is also in place for referrers: it does not block signups but prevents status changes while banned.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … the ban pause reactivation logic is also there for the referers as well. Um, same thing like it's it's not necessarily going to prevent any signups from coming in. Um, but uh it will it'll uh prevent statuses from moving when they're banned.

items.topic: Log signup screen required to reach In Progress
items.statement: Kobi reported that a signup moves to In Progress only when information is entered in the log signup screen; otherwise a warning shows and it stays New.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … the signup has also been updated so that you have to enter some information in the log signup screen for it to move to in progress. Um, otherwise there's a warning that says like, you know, nothing's been filled out. So, it's not it's going to remain as new.

items.topic: Integration groundwork; external ID includes sources
items.statement: Kobi reported that integration groundwork has started and the deal external ID and deal name logic now include the sources.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … started the integration groundwork. So, I think you already know about that one. Um, the deal electional ID and deal name logic to include the sources is in place.
items.asr_note: electional ID / delectional ID / de-electional ID = external ID [ASR?]

items.topic: Operator/partner page updates closed off
items.statement: Kobi reported a number of updates to the operator and partner pages, including rollups, and that Taryn updated the document to show what has been closed off.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … there are a number of updates done to the operator and partner pages as well like the rollups and everything. Um I believe Taryn updated the document to reflect what's been closed off.

items.topic: Emily to validate feedback and send outstanding object feedback
items.statement: Emily will go back through the items WagerTech sent feedback on, validate them so they can be closed, and send the feedback still owed on a few objects.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, I will kind of go back through everything that we like sent feedback on and kind of validate and then we can close out. / Emily Vandenberg: … I know that there's still a few objects that we owe you feedback on and that's like high in my priority as well. So that will, you know, be coming in today into next week.

items.topic: Start next-phase discovery next week
items.statement: Emily asked to agree that discovery for the next phase starts next week, and Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … I think part of my kind of like you know hope for next week is that we can start some of the discovery around the next phase. / Emily Vandenberg: So let's just like agree that like we we start that next week. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah.

items.topic: Do not resolve each SLC error from unset deals
items.statement: Errors on incoming study link clicks are caused by deals that are not set up yet. The team agreed not to resolve every error and to move on to sending deals from Salesforce to the CMS, which should resolve them.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … I know there's a lot of deals that are coming through right now that are like not having the the deals assigned um and you're getting a lot of kind of error codes. I think we know we know that the study link click is working like we know that the data is coming through. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … So, I'm good with this. We don't necessarily need to resolve every single error because I I the errors that are coming in is because we don't have those deals set up. And that's okay. Like, we already we're good with this. We can move on to the next stage, which is getting the deals sent from Salesforce to CMS.

items.topic: SLC flow validated when deal and DRA exist
items.statement: Kobi stated that testing validated that when the deal and deal rep assignment are set up and data comes from the CMS, the flow works.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … we know that you know if you have the deal set up and the deal rep assignment set up uh and the information comes from uh from CMS uh everything is working smoothly. I think that was like the main point of the sole testing. So, we validated that.

items.topic: Batch import of deals suggested
items.statement: Emily said she thinks a batch import of all deals is needed, followed by the Salesforce-to-CMS deal endpoint. No one confirmed the batch import.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … Like I think we just need to do a batch import of like everything and then we get the endpoint and like the communication between the deals working um Salesforce to the CMS

items.topic: Emily to compare click logs with Salesforce
items.statement: Emily will do another comparison of WagerTech click-log records against Salesforce records to confirm data still flows through for the two reps.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, I'll do another like cloud comparison against like the records from our click logs versus this just to like, you know, make sure that we're still everything's still flowing through for those two reps.

items.topic: Links sent with the deal payload
items.statement: Salesforce will send the links for a deal along with the deal; the initial idea is one payload with a sub-array of links under the deal. Strahinja accepted this.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: … Emily was saying along with the deal, you guys are going to be sending the links that are uh representing that deal, which is fine. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … we'll send it all in a uh in like one payload, right? Like you have the the deal and then you'll have a like a subarray underneath it for each link.

items.topic: CMS handling of link edit and delete
items.statement: Strahinja said the CMS will take an edited link at face value and will deactivate a deleted link (keeping it for tracking and reporting). Kobi accepted.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: … Like you can just edit a link, we'll take out face value. If you delete it, we'll deactivate it so we can keep uh keep it around for tracking reporting purposes. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I see it. Okay.

items.topic: Strahinja to draft link fields document
items.statement: Kobi asked for a table of expected link fields and unique identifiers so Jumpr can build the links object. Strahinja will draft a document similar to the deal one, with links carrying IDs.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … But for the links, uh it would be helpful to know what you're expecting in terms of fields like is there like a unique identifier? / Strahinja Vladetic: Oh yeah, I should be able to do the same. I think I think the main thing would be just to have the links so that we can support that workflow if if if the links could have uh ids along with them / Strahinja Vladetic: I'll uh but I'll I'll draft up another document similar to this one for that and that'll be sending the same payload,

items.topic: Single endpoint for deal and links
items.statement: Strahinja decided to keep one endpoint: Salesforce sends the payload and the CMS works out what changed. Kobi accepted.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: Yeah, to keep it simple, we'll probably just stick with the with the one endpoint and I can do the processing on my side to figure out what's changed. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay.
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier in this meeting Strahinja said a new endpoint would probably be added for inserting new links (line 232); this replaces that.

items.topic: Salesforce drives deal external ID
items.statement: Salesforce will drive the deal external ID. The CMS will trust whatever ID Salesforce sends and use it to reference the deal, including on SLC clicks sent back.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … For the delectional ID, are we good with um Salesforce driving the ID? So, whatever we send is what we end up using to send back with the SLC clicks. / Strahinja Vladetic: Yeah, 100%. / Strahinja Vladetic: … But once you guys take um take control of that, we'll just trust whatever you send back as the ID and then that's what we'll yeah that's how we'll reference it going forward.
items.asr_note: electional ID / delectional ID / de-electional ID = external ID [ASR?]

items.topic: Same-makeup lock blocks recreating mistaken deals
items.statement: The endpoint treats the same makeup as the same deal. If a deal is created by mistake and already has signups, a new deal with the same makeup cannot be created; Kobi raised this to define retire-and-replace handling.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … one of the enforcements that came out of the endpoint was if we send the same makeup, we're treating that as the same deal.

items.topic: CMS options A/B for deal retire-replace
items.statement: Strahinja deferred the retire-and-replace choice to Emily and Joyce but said he liked option B; he added option A can be automatic on the CMS side but is riskier, destructive and hard to undo. The options are not described in the transcript.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: Yeah, I think it's going to be more of a main question, so I'll probably defer to Emily and Joyce, but I like the option B um along with Vegas. / Strahinja Vladetic: we also could do option A and it doesn't have to be a manual process at least on not on the CMS side. Um it's a it's a little more risky and and destructive the only
items.asr_note: 'along with Vegas' unclear [ASR?]; 'main question' may be 'business question' [ASR?]

items.topic: Reactivated deal with new terms stays same deal
items.statement: Emily said a deal that deactivates and comes back with new commercial terms should be treated as a reactivation of the same deal, with the change logged. Kobi later restated this as a decision.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Like I think when the like the example of commercial terms like you know something deactivates it comes back with like new commercial terms like I would treat that as like just a reactivation and you're logging the change and you kind of like know but it's essentially the same deal. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … So decisions we're making is like ideally the deal remains the same even if it gets deactivated and reactivated at a later time.

items.topic: Must allow new deal with previously used makeup
items.statement: Emily said the system must not block creating a new deal with a makeup used before (for example a future BetMGM direct Jersey deal after an erroneous one), or WagerTech would be completely blocked.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … So like I don't want to say that could never happen, right? Like because in the future we will need to go potentially and have and assign a bet MGM direct jersey deal like that that will be / Emily Vandenberg: a scenario. And if we would have like been operating off of you know not having this kind of sorted and like it being not being able to create a new um deal for that because it was once deleted from like that unique makeup perspective like we would have been completely blocked.

items.topic: Incremental counter for duplicate external IDs exists
items.statement: Kobi said Salesforce already has logic to add an incremental counter to the external ID when a deal with the same makeup is created (e.g. a -001 suffix), so the CMS must accept Salesforce IDs as-is.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … we already have logic built in to add in like an incremental counter if somebody creates the same deal with the same makeup um that results in the same ID. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And then uh with Salesforce driving the external ids, as long as CMS is able to accept those as is, we're good there.

items.topic: Add Retired deal status
items.statement: Kobi proposed adding a Retired status (alongside Active, Inactive, Closed) so a mistaken or old deal can be retired and its makeup reused. Emily acknowledged ('Okay') but there was no explicit confirmation; design options are still to come.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … So, we can add like an additional status for like right now we have active, inactive, closed. We can add like a retired status which will help us in the case of like you know we created a deal by mistake with the makeup that we later need to use at another time / Kobi Kunasekaran: So the makeup, so the dduplication we will do based off of like the five fields that we talked about. um but only against active deals. So if a deal is retired, then it's not going to flag that there's already another deal with the same makeup. / Emily Vandenberg: Okay.

items.topic: Deal makeup de-duplication rule
items.statement: Kobi described the planned de-duplication: based on the five makeup fields, applied to all non-retired deals; creating a duplicate is blocked with a message to add assignments to the existing deal or retire it first. De-duplication is not enforced today.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But if if there is another deal with the same makeup, up that's active or in any of the other statuses, then when you try to create that deal, it'll block you from creating the deal and say that there's already an existing deal. Go look at that and see if you need to add like assignments to that um or retire it before creating a new one.

items.topic: Track commercial terms over time
items.statement: Emily said commercial terms must be tracked with start and end dates, can keep changing on the same deal, and the system must compute which terms applied to signups in each date range.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … my thinking Joyce here is that like we need to be able to track the commercial terms and it needs to like be start kind of like end right / Kobi Kunasekaran: … commercial terms can change and we do need to keep track of the commercial terms.

items.topic: Signup payout ties to terms at completion
items.statement: Joyce said each signup is a CPA conversion whose amount ties to the deal terms; she confirmed it is the terms in force when the signup was completed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: no, I'm just tying it back to like each each signup h is represents um a CPA for us, right? Like a conversion where we get paid and that conversion amount can only tie back to the terms set out at the deal level. / Kobi Kunasekaran: but only like the the commercial terms that were set on the deal at the time the signup was like completed / Joyce Kiddell: Correct.

items.topic: Commercial term fields that can change
items.statement: Fields that can change over a deal's life and must be tracked: CPA, caps, deposit range, average deposit target, and possibly payout model (e.g. rev share to flat).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … And is it just a CPA or are there any other fields here that could potentially change throughout the life cycle of the deal that we need to keep track of / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, like the cap's going to change and we're going to need to track that. Caps are kind of always um up for change. the deposit range and um average deposit and the deposit range and average deposit target like that can change / Joyce Kiddell: I would say basically anything in this box, right? M like payout model. I don't know how often this happens, but I feel like we should be prepared for like the possibility of it shifting from like a rev share to a flat.

items.topic: Currency change means new deal for now
items.statement: For now a currency change will be handled by creating a new deal rather than changing currency within a deal; changing currency on the same deal would need a further discussion.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I pinged her. Yeah, I think like for now it would be fine, but / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, maybe it's something that we don't deal with until we have to deal with it. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … If you want the same deal, like if you want the ability for the same deal to change the currency, that's when we'll have to have a chat. But uh we're okay with creating a new deal.

items.topic: Can currency change within a deal?
items.statement: Whether currency can change within a deal makeup is not confirmed; Joyce said it may need to be validated with Lina and Emily pinged her.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: do we want the ability to change currency within a deal makeup? / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, we might have to validate that one with Lena. / Emily Vandenberg: I pinged her.

items.topic: Do commercial terms need to go to CMS?
items.statement: Emily said commercial terms live in Salesforce only, but Strahinja said the CMS may need term history for reporting, depending on how much reporting happens in Salesforce. Not resolved.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … are these information are you expecting this data to also come into the CMS or is this just living on Salesforce from like a reporting perspective? / Emily Vandenberg: just Salesforce. / Strahinja Vladetic: I think I think it might need to come into the CMS if you guys wanted to report on it like

items.topic: Strahinja to investigate commercial terms reporting need
items.statement: Strahinja will investigate where WagerTech would benefit from commercial terms data in CMS reporting; WagerTech will take Kobi's recommendation away and get back to Jumpr.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: I'll I'll do a I'll just do a quick investigation to see where you would benefit from that in in the data and the potential reporting and then you guys can tell me if that is it going to end up in Salesforce or if you care about those scenarios. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. Okay. We We'll take that away and SH will take a look, / Emily Vandenberg: but and and we'll get back to you.

items.topic: Join Salesforce data at reporting layer
items.statement: Kobi recommended pushing fields to the CMS only if they drive CMS or agency-website logic; for reporting, use a data warehouse or BI connector to Salesforce (e.g. Snowflake) instead of the API. He noted API call limits but does not expect to hit them at current volume.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: like my my recommendation would be like if the if you need these fields to drive some sort of automation filter or any logic on the CMS or the agency website, let's push it through on the object. Otherwise, if you need it for reporting purposes, you don't necessarily like we don't necessarily need to use the API to send all the information back and forth / Kobi Kunasekaran: … Snowflake for example has a connector. Uh most data tools have a connector to Salesforce. You don't necessarily need to send the data through an API um just to have it for reporting.

items.topic: Snapshot deal terms onto signup at completion
items.statement: Kobi proposed stamping relevant deal fields (CPA and others) onto the signup record when it is marked Completed, since signup deal fields today are formulas showing current deal values.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … And the way we have this set up is that it's it's not it's not a snapshot of the deal at the time the signup is completed or anything like that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … So what I'm thinking is we need to start taking snapshots of the fields that are relevant from the deal onto the sign up and maybe put it behind the completed date. So once the signup is marked as completed, we pull CPA and anything else that's relevant from the deal and save it in the signup record itself.

items.topic: Payout/redeposit snapshots discussed next week
items.statement: Kobi said the same snapshot approach may be needed for payouts and redeposits, to be discussed next week.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … Maybe like we might have to do the same for like payouts and redeposits. We can talk about that next week.

items.topic: Deal versioning vs commercial terms object
items.statement: Strahinja and Emily raised versioning the deal per terms change. Kobi said both versioning and the alternatives have pros and cons and he will present options for a decision.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: So for all these these changes, would would it make sense for the deal to just be like versioned and then you'll just know for like which version was connected to which signups? / Kobi Kunasekaran: … It could like I think there there are pros and cons to both. I can I can maybe like do like a uh run the pros and cons of both and show you the options of and then we can decide on which way to move forward.

items.topic: Related Commercial Terms object with effective dates
items.statement: As an alternative to versioning, Kobi proposed a related Commercial Terms list with effective start and end dates, CPA and payout model; only one is active and it stamps onto the signup.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … but on the deal level in place of versioning the alternate is we have a related uh related list for the commercial terms. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … there's only going to be one that's active and the active one is going to be the one that gets passed on to the signup record.

items.topic: Backdated CPA changes with editable dates
items.statement: Emily said term changes must not be just timestamped at the time of change: effective dates should default to the change date but be editable, to support backdated CPA changes (e.g. a change learned 10 days into the month backdated to the 1st).
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … if I go to an example that happened yesterday is like we found out 10 days into the month that a CPA changed but it's they're backdating it to the first so you have to be able to go in and then like mark when the new / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Emily Vandenberg: one um you have to have the ability should probably default you know to like the the dates of you know when you're kind of like changing it but then the ability to edit

items.topic: Auto-update related signups on backdated CPA
items.statement: Kobi suggested that, with a commercial terms object, updating the CPA on an existing term could automatically update related signups.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … if we do the commercial terms related object we could have it so when you update the CPA for an existing commercial term any related signup for that commercial term also / Kobi Kunasekaran: gets updated with the latest CPA do it that way so you don't have to manually update

items.topic: Reassign signups from erroneous deal to corrected deal
items.statement: Emily asked how to correct a deal created in error so historical signups report against the corrected deal; she asked for a quick merge function. Kobi suggested a superseded field plus automation to reassign signups, but this is not committed; Emily asked for options and effort first.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Hey, saying like the signups that have come in in the direct version uh sorry in the old version should be reallocated to the new version so that when you report on it everything looks like it came from the new deal / Kobi Kunasekaran: … I think we talked about like a superseded field. So, if you mark that this deal takes over for another deal, um, you just relate it back. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, for me like what I was saying is like a quick functionality to merge. Like if it was an error, like you know what I mean? You can like merge. But maybe like think it through and just like kind of let us know what option and like effort looks like and we can take it from there.

items.topic: Deal merge touches multiple relationships
items.statement: Kobi noted merging/reassigning deals must be tested because it touches the deal makeup, the deal rep assignment makeup and, later, links and their relation to signups.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Yeah, I think like we'll have to try it out because it there's like multiple relationships that play here. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like there's the deal makeup, there's the deal rep assignment makeup and then once we start introducing the links, that's another layer

items.topic: Kobi to provide deal design options
items.statement: Kobi will provide design options (and effort) for handling changing commercial terms / versioning and the merge of corrected deals. He said this will not block the CMS integration.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … So, um yeah, I I'll think it through. I'll provide the option and we can go from there. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we're good. Yeah, and I'll get back to you on options on how we're going to design like the deal with the commercial terms changing and what that could look like, but I think I don't think that's going to block the CMS integration

items.topic: Kobi to send signup snapshot field list
items.statement: Kobi will make a list of deal / commercial term fields to snapshot on signup records and send it to WagerTech to confirm.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … I'll probably want to know like what information we want to capture on the signup records like a snapshot of the deal or the commercial terms. So, I I'll make a list and I'll I'll send it over and you can just confirm and we can get that added as well.

items.topic: Use CMS staging environment for integration build
items.statement: The CMS staging environment will be used for the integration build instead of production (no production traffic there); Jumpr will swap to production when ready for the full deals-to-SLC test.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Are we able to create a sandbox in the CMS for Kobe so that we can like and teams so we can start testing / Strahinja Vladetic: Yeah, we do have the staging environment. We've just been using production. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think that's okay for now / Kobi Kunasekaran: … I think once we're good with how the data goes into the sandbox or or your staging environment then we can swap it out when we're ready to do the full test right like from deals to uh to the SLC's coming in.

items.topic: Strahinja to share staging Postgres connection
items.statement: Kobi asked for direct query access to the CMS sandbox database, not only API credentials. Strahinja said it is a Postgres database and he will give Jumpr the connection; Kobi asked for sandbox info and access to start.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … is there like a database that we can query to see what's actually landing on it uh outside of the API calls and can we get access to that? / Strahinja Vladetic: Uh yeah, definitely. Yeah, it's it's stored in a Postgress database. So I can just give you guys the connection. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … So yeah, as soon as send us like the information for sandbox uh and access um we can start setting this up.

items.topic: Three-phase CMS integration plan
items.statement: Integration phases: (1) send deal information to the CMS, (2) add affiliate links, (3) deal rep assignments from the CMS to Salesforce, to be scoped once links are in.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … So first phase is like sending the deal information to the CMS. Second one is adding the affiliate links. / Kobi Kunasekaran: … And then the third step will be the DRRA assignments that come from the CMS to Salesforce. Um so we can scope that out once the links come in.

items.topic: Link endpoint takes array of IDed links
items.statement: Strahinja confirmed what the CMS needs from Jumpr for links is an array of links with IDs; Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: But what did you need from um jumper to like know what's needed there? / Strahinja Vladetic: It's really just going to be by the sounds of it an array of links that are IDed. That's That's pretty much it, I think. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I would think so.

items.topic: High-level deal-link-DRA process
items.statement: Agreed high-level flow: Salesforce sets up deals and links and sends them to the CMS; the CMS assigns links to reps; assignments go back to Salesforce, which creates deal rep assignment records and signups from SLCs.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: cuz we're still assuming that the process is like Salesforce, we set up the deals and the links get sent to CMS and on CMS side, you're assigning those links. for those deals to the reps that you already have. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And when those assignments are done, that gets sent back to Salesforce, which kind of closes the loop and creates the deal rep assignment records and the signup records based off of the SLC's. Right? That's the process from a high level. / Strahinja Vladetic: Yep.

items.topic: Frequent DRA changes handling deferred
items.statement: Emily raised that rep assignments change often and asked how Salesforce will handle those CMS messages (versioning/logging). Kobi deferred this until links are in place; current focus is deals and affiliate links. Emily agreed it still needs a discussion.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: … Those are assignments can change quite frequently. Um, so just managing those messages and and sends from the CMS to back to you guys and I guess how you'll handle that from like a version or / Kobi Kunasekaran: … Uh yeah, we we can talk through it when we get to that base. Uh but right now I think focus is deals and affiliate links and that'll get us to the next step. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. Yeah. I think you're right though. We do need to chat through that.

items.topic: New links created in Salesforce first
items.statement: Reps will add brand-new links in Salesforce before assigning them in the CMS. If CMS-side link creation is needed later, it will be discussed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Are you expecting reps to be able to add links in CMS directly or would they still go to Salesforce to add the links before they assign it in CMS? / Emily Vandenberg: like a brand new link. So we get we would follow the process of adding the link in sales. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. We'll we'll we'll move forward with with that assumption and then if we if we need to enable a way for them to do it from CMS as well, if it's easier, then we can talk through what that looks like.

items.topic: Operators/partners sent in deal payload; CMS trusts Salesforce
items.statement: No new operator/partner endpoint: operator and partner (with IDs) go in the deal message, and the CMS trusts Salesforce completely, provisioning or assigning them and overwriting existing data. The unknown operator/partner error is crossed out.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … Is that going to be a new endpoint? How frequently does this happen to warrant a new endpoint or are we good with just sending it as part of the deal makeup / Strahinja Vladetic: … We just trust Salesforce completely and they send along the operator and partner along with their IDs and whatever information you guys want to keep in in the CMS and then the deal. / Strahinja Vladetic: We just overwrite whatever we have um existing. Yeah, in that scenario, this should never happen. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Okay. So, we can cross this one out.

items.topic: CMS operators tab may be retired
items.statement: Strahinja said the CMS has an operators tab that could be retired if Salesforce manages operators. Emily noted that tab really holds the short code, an early form of deal makeup. No decision to retire it.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: Yeah, the thing is right now we do have an operators tab in the CMS. / Strahinja Vladetic: moved. gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Deal lifecycle design decisions finalized with new retired status and commercial terms table.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … but on the deal level in place of versioning the alternate is we have a related uh related list for the commercial terms. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we're good. Yeah, and I'll get back to you on options on how we're going to design like the deal with the commercial terms changing and what that could look like
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript. The commercial terms table is one of several options Kobi proposed; he will come back with options (lines 406, 469, 583). The Gemini Decisions section itself lists this as 'Needs Further Discussion'.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Addition of retired deal status A retired status will be added to deal records to prevent duplication errors and handle reactivations or corrections.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: … So, we can add like an additional status for like right now we have active, inactive, closed. We can add like a retired status which will help us in the case of like you know we created a deal by mistake with the makeup that we later need to use at another time
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript. Kobi proposed it ('we can add'); Emily only said 'Okay' after the de-dup explanation (line 435) and asked for options and effort on the correction flow. Also, Emily said reactivations stay the same deal (line 278), so 'handle reactivations' via retired status is not supported.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Strahinja confirmed the team has access to the Postgres database to query results directly outside of API calls.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Strahinja Vladetic: Uh yeah, definitely. Yeah, it's it's stored in a Postgress database. So I can just give you guys the connection.
gemini_disagreements.why: Access is not in place yet. Strahinja agreed to provide the connection; Kobi still asked for sandbox info and access at line 581.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Strahinja noted the CMS will retire its internal operator and partner tabs, deferring to Salesforce as the system of record.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Strahinja Vladetic: moved. If if sales if Salesforce is going to be like the thing that manages that then we can just retire that in the CMS Yes.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript. Strahinja's statement is conditional, only an operators tab is mentioned, and Emily said the tab really holds the short code / early deal makeup (line 561). No decision to retire it.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Salesforce data synchronization established for operators and partners.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Strahinja Vladetic: So I'll update the payload with basically the to give you guys room to send me links and then send me the operators and partners with some basic information for now.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript. The approach was agreed, but nothing is established yet; Strahinja still has to update the payload.
